name: Hey Healthcare
outcome: inactive per YC; shutdown year unknown
founder_evidence: Andrew Coyle previously worked in interaction design at Google and Intuit and was Flexport's founding designer and director of design.
Evelyn Gillie was Flexport's director of engineering before Hey Healthcare and earned Stanford BS and MS degrees in symbolic systems and computer science.

name: Algen Biotechnologies
founder_evidence: Chun-Hao Huang earned his PhD through Memorial Sloan Kettering/Weill Cornell and developed CRISPR technologies as a Berkeley postdoctoral researcher in Jennifer Doudna's laboratory.
Christine Du trained as a scientist, worked across academic research and biotechnology commercialization, and earned a Wharton MBA focused on healthcare management.
Spencer Knight, identified as a co-founder by Berkeley and General Atlantic, earned a Berkeley PhD in chemistry and chemical biology and began his career as a Foresite Capital data scientist.

name: Webflow
founder_evidence: Sergie Magdalin was a professional designer who collaborated with Vlad on client websites before building Webflow.
Vlad Magdalin coded websites, operated a web-design agency, and worked at Intuit before turning his longstanding visual-development project into Webflow.
Bryant Chou worked with Vlad at Intuit building enterprise SaaS software and joined Webflow as its technical co-founder in early 2013.

name: HelpNow
outcome: inactive per YC; shutdown year unconfirmed
founder_evidence: Shikhar Agrawal developed HelpNow with Aditya while studying engineering at IIT Bombay, initially entering the idea in its EUREKA competition.
Venkatesh Amrutwar earned an IIT Bombay civil-engineering degree, worked as a business analyst at Quantum Phinance, and co-founded RoadCare before joining HelpNow.
Aditya Makkar was an IIT Bombay engineering student whose father's ambulance emergency motivated the venture, which operated ambulances in Mumbai in 2019.

name: LendEDU
founder_evidence: Matthew Lenhard was a University of Delaware student who co-founded ShopTutors and programmed LendEDU after the team abandoned tutoring in 2014.
Nate Matherson was a University of Delaware student and ShopTutors co-founder who led LendEDU's business development and marketing after experiencing student-loan refinancing difficulties.

name: Bicycle AI
founder_evidence: Arpit Mohan earned a BITS Pilani electrical-and-electronics engineering degree, co-founded Gharpay, and held engineering roles at Clinknow, Ezetap and Exotel before Bicycle AI.
Abhishek Nayak studied at BITS Pilani and previously founded Gharpay and Clink, acquired by Delhivery and Ezetap respectively, before serving as Bicycle AI's CEO.
Arvind Singh was Bicycle AI's co-founder and chief scientific officer; the reviewed sources did not establish his earlier employers or education.

name: Noora Health
founder_evidence: Edith Elliott studied international policy and global health at Stanford and worked on HIV, malaria and safe-water programs before co-founding Noora.
Shahed Alam studied biomedical engineering and public health at Johns Hopkins and medicine at Stanford, with prior research on healthcare access and low-cost diagnostics.
Katy Ashe earned two Stanford engineering degrees and conducted health research and community organizing concerning illegal gold mining in the Amazon before Noora.
Jessie Liu was a Stanford medical student and former Fulbright scholar who joined the other three founders through Stanford's Design for Extreme Affordability course.

name: FanHero
outcome: shut down; FanHero product abandoned in 2013, corporate closure year unknown
founder_evidence: Charlie Guo earned a Stanford computer-science degree and previously co-founded ClassOwl, a StartX-backed education startup; he explicitly reported having no creator-industry experience.
Kevin Xu was Guo's Stanford computer-science classmate and designer/developer co-founder; their programming-education idea became FanHero during YC, and his Stripe engineering work came afterward.

name: Paribus
founder_evidence: Karim Atiyeh earned Harvard degrees in electrical engineering and computer science before co-founding Paribus, his first company.
Eric Glyman earned a Harvard degree in economics and East Asian studies and co-founded Paribus with Atiyeh.

name: Byte
outcome: inactive per YC; shutdown year unknown
founder_evidence: Safee Shah led Uber Pakistan, previously worked in investment management at Timescape Capital Management and Corey Macro Management, and holds a LUMS bachelor's degree and Emory MBA; his Harvard credential is online executive education rather than a degree.
